policy.title:
HOLY HELL! January's stablecoin volume hit $10.3T.

(Last year's ENTIRE annual volume was $33T!)

We
policy.description:
HOLY HELL! January's stablecoin volume hit $10.3T.

(Last year's ENTIRE annual volume was $33T!)

We just did nearly a THIRD of that in 30 days.

$USDC alone processed $8.4T in January.

That's more than double Visa's entire Q1 payment volume of $4T.

- $USDT added another $1.8T.
- $DAI at $58.1B.
- $USDS at $57.7B.

The use of tokenized dollars is scaling faster than anyone expected.

And I know, I know - stablecoins are stable (and that makes them boring)…

But this isn't about stablecoins. It's about the pipes.

RWAs are the most important sector in crypto right now.

The higher RWAs clims, the more of global finance gets tokenized.

The more gets tokenized, the more structural demand exists for the chains processing these transactions.

(And with that, demand for their native tokens to pay fees).

The top 5 winners for January, by chain, were:

- Base $5.8T (uses ETH for gas fees)
- Ethereum $2.2T (uses ETH for gas fees)
- Tron $672.0B (uses TRX for gas fees)
- Solana 490.1B (uses SOL for gas fees)
- BNB Chain 389.0B (uses BNB for gas fees)

We’re watching whether February sustains this pace.

If it does, the "crypto has no real world use case” narrative is going to start aging worse than it already is.

company.description:
🧵 XDC Network and BitGo
A real institutional milestone

@XDCNetwork has secured institutional custody support with @BitGo. 
This is a major step toward regulated, real-world on-chain adoption.

With this integration, $XDC and $USDC can now be held under BitGo’s regulated custody framework.
That matters because custody is often the first hard blocker for institutions.

Institutions do not move capital on-chain without secure, compliant, and trusted custody.
This is not about hype.
It is about infrastructure.

BitGo provides regulated MPC custody through BitGo Bank and Trust, designed specifically for institutional requirements such as compliance, security, and governance.

This unlocks access for enterprises, exchanges, and financial institutions that require bank-grade custody before deploying real capital on a blockchain.

The inclusion of USDC is equally important.
Settlement liquidity and stablecoin access are critical for real usage, especially in trade finance and cross-border flows.

XDC Network has long focused on trade finance, cross-border payments, and tokenized real-world assets.
Those use cases demand regulated rails, not experimental setups.

Another important signal
BitGo is not just a custodian.
It is a regulated Trust Bank and also a member of the Hedera Governing Council, where it operates infrastructure at the network governance level.

That positioning reinforces BitGo’s focus on institutional-grade, compliance-first digital asset infrastructure across multiple ecosystems.

Takeaway
Adoption does not start with price.
It starts with custody, settlement, compliance, and trust.

When institutions move on-chain, this is what it looks like
Regulated custody first
Liquidity and stablecoins next
Real volume follows later

👉🏻 https://t.co/3iSBumQBEU

Regulated stablecoins are finally entering the scene, and it's a game-changer 🚀💰 

Tether's USAT is
company.description:
Regulated stablecoins are finally entering the scene, and it's a game-changer 🚀💰 

Tether's USAT is the first federally regulated U.S. stablecoin, issued by Anchorage Digital Bank under OCC oversight. Backed 1:1 by USD, custodied by Cantor Fitzgerald, and compliant with the GENIUS Act, available on top exchanges like Bybit, Kraken, OKX, https://t.co/vs0s7DItqA, Moonpay. 

Fidelity steps in with FIDD, their USD-backed stablecoin on Ethereum, accessible to both retail and institutional clients. Reserves? Cash, cash equivalents, and short-term Treasuries, with daily public attestations. 

Both are paving the way for clear regulatory guardrails in crypto payments. The future of stablecoins is regulated, safe, and legit 🔒✨. 

Are you ready to leverage this new wave of stability?
